why: The criterion holds. I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests that padLeft is exported, pads on the left, uses fill or a space when fill is left out, and reaches width ("00042", "  ab", "**x"). Those are just cases the words already demand. Check 2 needs '"abc" "abcdef" "abcdef"' to come back unchanged, which is exactly what the line says. Check 3 asks for "a heading that names it with text about it" for every exported function. That is a fair reading of "section", and it does not require any heading format. Check 4 passes when npm test "exits 0 with no failing tests". The stricter items all sit under "Advisory (not PASS/FAIL conditions)": whether the tests cover padLeft, whether headings follow the `## name(args)` style, and whether the other functions behave as before. None of the checks requires mutation tests, a branch or file scope, or exact wording.
